profile.name: health_only
profile.policy: Freeze the profile and required targets before final-data examination. health_only needs no social head or retrieval evidence. joint_health_retrieval additionally requires trained social embeddings and independent retrieval evidence. Optional diagnostics cannot replace required targets after inspection.

scope.operation: metrics-only over externally supplied predictions and human labels

bootstrap.interval_scope: Report central two-sided 95% intervals and one-sided 95% lower/upper bounds per metric. Directional gates use the one-sided bounds. The predeclared required gates form an intersection; successful targets cannot be selected after inspection.
bootstrap.degenerate_replicates: retain undefined denominators as null; do not silently discard; an affected interval is not evaluable
bootstrap.decision_flip_acceptance_bound: For one row per independent author, use an exact one-sided 95% binomial upper bound, including a positive upper bound when no flips are observed. Cross-author independence still requires design review. For repeated-author samples use the paired author-cluster percentile upper bound only away from zero/all-flip boundaries; boundary acceptance remains not_evaluable. Preserve the bootstrap interval separately as a diagnostic.
limitations: Authors are resampled with replacement and all their evaluated rows remain together.
The same resampled author groups are used for reference, candidate and their paired difference.
This does not account for correlations between different authors, conversations, events or time blocks.
A design review must address remaining dependence before qualification.
Small or homogeneous samples can produce misleadingly narrow or degenerate intervals; planning counts do not certify coverage or power.

precision_plan.nullable_criteria_policy: A frozen precision-review artifact must explain the chosen sample/author design and usable uncertainty. Null additional author-count or interval-width limits are not automatic passes; they are only not-applicable criteria when the predeclared review explicitly justifies the design. Without the review digest evaluation remains not_evaluable.

annotation_agreement.policy: An externally supplied agreement receipt must be based on a new independent pre-adjudication sample, include a rubric-independent annotator, raw agreement, class counts, missing/insufficient labels and uncertainty. This executor validates and records that receipt but does not recompute alpha without the original ratings.

calibration.policy: Brier score and fixed-bin expected calibration error are computed. A predeclared external calibration/slice regression review is required when no numeric Brier tolerance has been specified. Unknown regression evidence is not a pass.

runtime_qualification.policy: Predictions must identify actual execution on the intended x86 target instruction set/runtime. Metadata is recorded external evidence, not a performance measurement made by this evaluator.

politicalness.definition: The text is about politics, government, elections, or public policy.

outraged.definition: The author expresses anger, indignation, or outrage.

critical.definition: The author attacks, condemns, or disparages a person, group, or institution; neutral disagreement alone is insufficient.

engagement_bait.definition: The author manipulates readers into replying, liking, or sharing mainly to increase engagement.

spam.definition: The text is unsolicited or repetitive promotional spam, a scam, or deceptive advertising.

heat.condition: No trained heat output exists in v3. Evaluation requires a frozen human heat definition, a direct independent human heat label, and an explicitly frozen aggregation on outraged and critical. No default max is implied.

retrieval.recall_definition: Per query: distinct relevant IDs in the first K ranked IDs divided by all adjudicated relevant IDs; report the macro average across queries.
retrieval.cosine_definition: Re-normalize each 256, 128 or 64 prefix of the supplied 256-vector, compute paired cosine, and report the empirical first percentile using linear interpolation.
retrieval.tail_caveat: The empirical p1 cosine is a sample-tail diagnostic; its stability depends on sample size and dependence. It does not establish retrieval quality.

design_notes: The governing remediation plan adopts these provisional minimum design gates before new labels. They are not promises of a confidence-interval width, statistical power or a probability of passing.

The positive target may be unattainable in a natural sample for rare labels. Additional enriched review can study rare failures, but its unweighted precision and F1 describe the enriched pool rather than deployment prevalence.
This executable reports sample-pool metrics. It does not implement inverse-inclusion-probability survey estimators and will not qualify enriched or convenience samples as population evidence.
Precision depends on prevalence and the false-positive rate; positive counts alone do not determine F1 uncertainty.
Report positives, negatives, unique authors, repeated-author counts, effective resampling unit, time range and language exclusions for every run.
Repeated authors reduce independent information. Author-cluster resampling preserves within-author dependence but cannot remove shared-event or conversational dependence across authors.
Freeze thresholds and any heat aggregation using development data before inspecting final predictions or labels. A final set is not a threshold-tuning set.
Use the initial double-labeled sample to diagnose ambiguity, disagreement and adjudication rules; 200 double labels do not certify the whole label bank.
Record achieved intervals and prevalence after labeling. Expand or redesign the sample based on a predeclared precision review, without repeatedly peeking at a final acceptance set.
A natural four-week sample studies a bounded time period; it does not establish future drift robustness, all-language quality, or production user outcomes.
Any reviewer-provided synthetic calculations remain design illustrations and must never be recorded as measured model evidence.

historical_smoke.policy: Read-only historical diagnostic; this contract never changes earlier smoke gates or receipts.
historical_smoke.max_absolute_probability_delta: Always reported as a diagnostic. New acceptance uses frozen decisions, paired metric intervals and retrieval parity only after tolerances are explicitly approved.

method_references.title: NIST Exact Binomial Confidence Limits
method_references.use: One-sided exact binomial CDF inversion for decision flips only when there is one row per independent author. Zero observed flips do not imply a zero upper confidence bound.

method_references.title: Statistical Significance Tests for Machine Translation Evaluation
method_references.use: Paired resampling compares systems on the same sampled observations; this evaluator adapts the pairing to author clusters.

method_references.title: Bootstrap-Based Improvements for Inference with Clustered Errors
method_references.use: Clustered observations require resampling that respects the sampling unit; no claim is made that this percentile implementation has the paper's bootstrap-t refinements.

method_references.title: Precision/Recall on Imbalanced Test Data
method_references.use: Prevalence and annotation sampling design affect precision/recall estimation; planning row counts alone are insufficient.
